proposals.evidence: Turner *hastakūṭa explicitly gives Punjabi/Lahnda hathoṛā, Nepali hothro, Bengali hātuṛi, Gujarati hathɔṛɔ/athɔṛɔ and Marathi hatoḍā. These survey hammer forms fit that established family, including initial h-loss, retroflex r/ḍ and regional vowel contraction. The severely shortened ṭhoṛā forms are qualified comparisons with the local hathoṛā family; unrelated hammer responses and mixed alternatives are excluded.

proposals.evidence: Turner musala explicitly supplies Gujarati musḷũ, Marathi musaḷ, Punjabi muhlā/mohlā and Sindhi muhurī pestle. The h/s forms and local contractions in these survey responses are compared with that regional musala family, with s > h and reduction preserved in the source spelling. Turner treats the word as probably non-Aryan in ultimate origin; this link does not invent an immediate Dravidian donor.
